findings.title: Another pod holds the ReadWriteOncePod claim
findings.cause: the pod mounts PersistentVolumeClaim data, whose access mode ReadWriteOncePod lets only one pod in the cluster use it, and pod db-56f8666648-5dbg8 already does, so the scheduler keeps this one Pending; Deployment db has 1 of 2 replicas ready

evidence.detail: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) unavailable due to PersistentVolumeClaim with ReadWriteOncePod access mode already in-use by another pod. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 No preemption victims found for incoming pod.

evidence.what: PersistentVolumeClaim data has access mode ReadWriteOncePod
evidence.command: kubectl get pvc data -n kd-rwop-claim-in-use -o jsonpath='{.spec.accessModes}'

evidence.what: pod db-56f8666648-5dbg8 mounts data on node kd-faults-control-plane
evidence.command: kubectl get pod db-56f8666648-5dbg8 -n kd-rwop-claim-in-use -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}'

findings.fix: Run one replica of Deployment db (a claim per replica needs a StatefulSet's volumeClaimTemplates), or use ReadWriteOnce if pods on one node may share the volume; with a rolling update, use strategy Recreate so the old pod lets go of the claim first.
